clue.text: Surprise to get uncapped wine

indicators.note: with its cap, the top letter, taken off the word for surprise

parts.note: to surprise is to shock

explanation.surface: A shock at being handed a bottle of wine without its cork or cap.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is a British name for German white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is a white Rhenish wine, so it is an example of the category named.

clue.text: That guy's hopeless, ignoring article about the liver

parts.note: 'that guy is' gives the pronoun he

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the article from the word for hopeless

parts.note: hopeless means pathetic
the definite article, the

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on some man who is useless and pays no attention to an article on the liver.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepatic is the medical adjective relating to the liver, from the Greek hepar.

clue.text: Be jubilant over new expensive headgear

indicators.note: in a down answer, the jubilant word sits over the abbreviation for new

parts.note: to crow is to boast or exult

explanation.surface: Someone gloating over a pricey new hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown is a monarch's jewelled head-dress, about the costliest headwear there is.

clue.text: Theatre-worker's hour after time moving into position

indicators.note: the time-and-hour pair is moved into the middle of the word for position

parts.note: a stand is a position, as in taking a stand

indicators.note: the abbreviation for hour comes after the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A backstage worker taking up a spot an hour after the call time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in Theatre-worker's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagehand moves scenery and props in a theatre, a backstage crew member.

clue.text: It's no great age: still time to get noticed externally

indicators.note: the word for noticed goes on the outside of the other letters

parts.note: noticed means seen
still, as in calm, means even

explanation.surface: Someone young still has time to be spotted by the world outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventeen years old is youthful, hardly an advanced age, hence the understated description.

clue.text: Cancel regular publication, missing one source of argument …

indicators.note: missing one means a single letter is left out of the publication

parts.note: an annual is a book published every year

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of argument, where it starts

explanation.surface: A call to scrap a periodical, short of a single trigger for debate.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, so it is a synonym for cancel.

clue.text: … English pound provided that, free to vary, not vacantly showing identical variability

parts.note: a quid is slang for a pound sterling
provided that means if

indicators.note: the letters are free to vary, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: vacantly means emptying the word not of its middle, keeping its outer letters

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a muddled statement about money and freedom showing sameness of variation.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the one before, making one running sentence that is really two separate clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Equidifferent describes a series whose successive terms differ by equal amounts, a technical term from arithmetic.

clue.text: Air of trio playing — more sound?

definitions.note: the phrase means with stronger reason, a more sound argument; the question mark flags the musical misdirection

indicators.note: musicians playing an air arrange its parts, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tune performed by a trio, and is there extra sound?
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks musical after 'Air' and 'trio', but here it means valid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase introduces a conclusion that follows with even greater force, so the reasoning is more sound.

clue.text: Misrepresent a lot of party upset over legal wrong

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits over the legal wrong in the down answer
in a down clue upset turns the letters bottom to top
most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A political party twisting things after a legal wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a political faction, but here it is one side in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To distort the facts is to twist them, giving a false account.

clue.text: In favour of turning in coalmine dividend

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the coalmine

parts.note: a pit is a coalmine

indicators.note: turning means the word for in favour of is read backwards

parts.note: in favour of means for

explanation.surface: Backing a share payout from a mining company.
explanation.definitionFit: A dividend is a share of a company's earnings, i.e. profit paid out to shareholders.

clue.text: Devours tuna melts, keen to try something unusual?

indicators.note: a tuna melt is a dish, but here melts means the letters are broken down and recast

explanation.surface: Someone eating tuna melts with gusto, as if open to culinary experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurous person is daring and eager for new experiences.

clue.text: Start to develop interpretation after a lot of brute criticism

indicators.note: the start letter and interpretation come after the shortened brute
most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a brute is an animal

indicators.note: the first letter of develop

parts.note: a version is an interpretation or account

explanation.surface: Reviewers begin to develop a reading after much harsh condemnation.
explanation.definitionFit: Animadversion is a formal word for censure or a critical remark.

clue.text: Crudely insolent about article regarding stress

indicators.note: the reworked letters go about the article
crudely means roughly put together, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A rude, cheeky remark about some magazine article on stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Tensional is the adjective for tension, relating to stress or strain.

clue.text: Excessive documentation returned, leading to more of the same

indicators.note: returned means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, excessive
ID means identity documents

explanation.surface: Too much paperwork sent back, prompting yet more forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto signals a repeat of what came before, the same again.

clue.text: Bread from birdhouse Mark's brought into lounge

indicators.note: the mark is brought into the birdhouse

parts.note: a cote is a shelter for doves or birds
a tag is a mark or label; the 's is 'is'
to loaf is to lounge about

explanation.surface: A loaf baked from a recipe found in a dovecote, Mark having brought it into the sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage loaf is a traditional British bread with a small round on top of a larger one.

clue.text: Quantity of beer popular with doctor, say? It sets the tone

parts.note: a tun is a large cask, a quantity of beer
popular means in
GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
say means for example, eg

explanation.surface: A pint and popularity for a family doctor, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a family doctor in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuning peg on a stringed instrument is turned to adjust the pitch of a string.

clue.text: Commotion, with lecturer interrupting worried boy rudely

indicators.note: the commotion and lecturer interrupt the rearranged boy
worried means agitated, so the letters of boy are shaken up
with joins the lecturer to the commotion

parts.note: making a scene is causing a commotion

explanation.surface: A fuss as a teacher breaks in on an anxious lad, rather impolitely.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscenely means in a coarse, indecent manner, a strong form of rudeness.

clue.text: See 16
Develop move in cinematography

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to turn ... or progress, as events do
second meaning: a camera sweep widening ... from a subject

explanation.walkthrough: Photography links 'develop' and cinematography in the surface, but 'develop' is meant as how things turn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to work out or turn out, and literally describes a camera panning outward.

clue.text: Style of hair that's something difficult to achieve with dog

indicators.note: with sets the dog word after the first piece

parts.note: a pig of a job is something hard to do
to dog is to follow, tail

explanation.surface: A hairdo that is hard to manage on a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigtail is a plait or bunch of hair hanging from the head.

clue.text: Unveils most of model after recasting statue

indicators.note: recasting, as with a statue, means reshaping the letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of the word, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A sculptor unveils a new statue after recasting most of the model.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venus de Milo is a famous ancient Greek marble statue in the Louvre.

clue.text: Ask too much of public — a sign of error

parts.note: overt means open, public
a cross, X, marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: Overburdening the public, a mark of a misjudgement.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtax is to make excessive demands on someone, a figurative strain.

clue.text: German holding on? He's not holding on

indicators.note: holding means the abbreviation for German wraps around the word on

explanation.surface: A German clings on, while another man lets go.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'holding on' is the trick: first it builds the wordplay, then it defines someone beyond saving.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone doomed or as good as dead, who cannot cling on any longer.

clue.text: The official or executive finally delivering in that case

parts.note: taken as written
a ref is a referee, a match official
taken as written

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of executive

explanation.surface: A referee or executive at last giving a verdict on the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore means consequently, for that reason, so introduces a conclusion.

clue.text: Fish — trawler disposing of contents into the drink

indicators.note: the emptied trawler goes into the drink

parts.note: tea is a drink

indicators.note: the trawler empties out, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: a fishing boat

explanation.surface: A trawler dumps its catch into the sea, the fish going overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is slang for the sea, but here the drink is tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Not wanting to eat anything? Not quite — tripe etc will suffice

parts.note: to be off one's food is to have no appetite

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: all, as in anything at all

explanation.surface: A fussy eater refuses everything, though tripe will do.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the edible internal organs of an animal, such as tripe, liver and kidneys.

clue.text: Leaders of troops filling suitable job

indicators.note: the leaders fill the word for suitable

parts.note: apt means suitable
point men lead a patrol of soldiers

explanation.surface: The heads of the army taking on a fitting post.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointment is a position or post, a job someone is appointed to.

clue.text: See 8
Fabulous support given to finish a railway

parts.note: a leg supports a table
end means finish

explanation.surface: Help offered to complete a railway line, which turns out wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary and fabulous both mean the stuff of myth and fable, or simply marvellous.

clue.text: Source of fibres, fine and loose

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
lax means loose or slack

explanation.surface: A source of fibre that is both delicate and loosely spun.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is the plant whose stem fibres are spun into linen.
